description: Guided C2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Abject begins with /æ/. Eject begins with /iː/; object and subject have different first-syllable vowel qualities and stress.
Quell has /ɛ/. Quill has /ɪ/, quail has /eɪ/, and qualm has /ɑ/.
Sullen begins with /ʌ/. Salon begins with /ə/, silken with /ɪ/, and solemn with /ɑ/.
Rhapsody begins with /r/; its written rh represents /r/. Lapse begins with /l/, haps with /h/, and dapper with /d/.
Chrysalis begins with /k/ because ch represents /k/. Shrewd begins with /ʃ/, gregarious with /g/, and syringe with /s/.
Wrangle begins with /r/ because its written w is silent. Wangle begins with /w/, jangle with /dʒ/, and mangle with /m/.
Bursts ends with /sts/. Burst and bust end with /st/, while bursary ends with a vowel sequence.
Waltzed ends with /tst/. Waltz ends with /ts/, waltzes with /ɪz/, and waltzing with /ɪŋ/.
Throbs ends with /bz/. Throb ends with /b/, throbbing with /bɪŋ/, and throbbed ends with /bd/.
Colonel is pronounced /ˈkɜrnəl/, an irregular spelling. The alternatives have different syllable patterns.
Segue is pronounced /ˈsɛɡweɪ/. Sequel ends with /əl/, sequin with /ɪn/, and sequester with /ɛstər/.
Indict is pronounced /ɪnˈdaɪt/; c is silent. The alternatives have different stress and vowel sequences.
